about: Schemas dossiq registers that nothing shows. A registered schema is storage: the instance creates it, the descriptor promises the capability, and no page, controller or service ever touches it. An entry names the slug, the change that registered it, and what has to happen before it can go. An entry without an ownerChange or a readerApp is not an entry: SchemaHasSurfaceTest fails on it. The list also fails in the OTHER direction, on a slug that has since gained a surface, so the number can only go down deliberately.
measuredBy: SchemaSurfaceScanner over lib/Settings/dossiq_register.json plus register.d/*.json: 166 schemas declared, 0 with no surface. It read 16 on the day it was written; fifteen of those were real and got pages, and the sixteenth was the scanner's own false positive.
triage: EMPTY, AND ONE OF THE SIXTEEN WAS NEVER DARK. `case-location` was reported as having no reader and it had one all along: CaseLocationMap fetches it, scoped to the case, from the Locations section of the case page. The slug sits inside an object URL rather than on its own, and the scanner only looked for a bare quoted slug. A change to build it a surface was queued off that report, which is the cost of an instrument that calls a working surface dark: somebody builds the thing a second time. The scanner now reads the URL shape, anchored at both ends so a slug that is a PREFIX of another is not carried by its neighbour. The other fifteen were real and have pages (#2958, #2959, #2961). NOTHING WAS RETIRED: each traced to a change that shipped its storage and its seeds and never shipped its page, so deleting it would destroy rows on any instance that has been filling it since June. The empty retire column was a finding, not a step that was skipped.
